title: Beyond the Kagome Layer: Interlayer Origin of the Flat Band in FeSn
authors: Shimin Zhang, Bipasa Samanta, Ho Viet Thang, Alexandru B. Georgescu
abstract: Kagome FeSn exhibits an occupied flat band at its terminated surface, whereas bulk FeSn adopts A-type antiferromagnetic order and does not display the same feature. Here, we combine density functional theory with primitive- and doubled-cell analysis and a double-layer tight-binding model to determine how interlayer electronic coupling and magnetic stacking control flat-band formation in FeSn. We identify an occupied Fe-$d_{z^2}$-derived flat-band manifold in the ferromagnetic state that is consistent with the experimentally observed surface feature. Brillouin-zone folding reveals that its flat branch originates from the $k_z=\fracπ{c}$ sector of the primitive cell, demonstrating that it cannot be understood as an isolated kagome-layer state. Instead, the state depends on coupling between neighboring kagome layers and can be seen as a result of antibonding coupling between nearest neighbor kagome layers. A double-layer tight-binding analysis identifies interlayer Fe-Fe hopping as the dominant microscopic coupling responsible for this behavior, while a contrasting unoccupied flat-band-related manifold is governed primarily by intralayer Fe-Sn hybridization. These results establish interlayer coupling and magnetic stacking as key control parameters for kagome flat bands and highlight how coupling between layers can generate and tune extended correlated-electron states in quantum materials.
summary: This work investigates the origin of flat bands in FeSn by combining DFT calculations with a double-layer tight-binding model. The study concludes that the experimentally relevant flat band is not an isolated layer feature but arises specifically from strong interlayer Fe-Fe coupling in the ferromagnetic state. This highlights that interlayer coupling and magnetic stacking are crucial parameters for tuning correlated electronic states in quantum materials.
main_problem: The study aims to determine how interlayer electronic coupling and magnetic stacking control the formation of flat bands in FeSn, particularly contrasting the surface-observed flat band with the bulk electronic structure.
main_result: The occupied flat band observed at the surface is shown to originate from interlayer Fe-Fe coupling in the ferromagnetic state, confirming that interlayer coupling is a key control parameter for these correlated electron states.
method: The research combines Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations with the construction and analysis of an effective double-layer tight-binding model.
model_or_system: The physical system is FeSn, featuring Kagome layers. The analysis uses DFT to calculate band structures under different magnetic orders (AFM, FM, NM) and employs a tight-binding model to separate contributions from intralayer (Fe-Sn) and interlayer (Fe-Fe) hopping.
key_observables: Flat-band features (specifically the 'A-lift' and 'bump-like' manifold), electronic band structures, and Projected Density of States (PDOS).
important_parameters: Interlayer Fe-Fe hopping strength, magnetic stacking (FM vs. AFM), and the specific Brillouin zone sector ($k_z = \pi/c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the surface termination breaks the inversion symmetry present in the bulk AFM environment, and the tight-binding model simplifies hopping amplitudes to independent parameters.
figures_summary: Figures compare DFT band structures for different magnetic states (AFM, FM, NM) and illustrate the folding of the band structure when comparing primitive vs. doubled unit cells. The tight-binding analysis maps the A-lift to interlayer coupling and the bump-like feature to intralayer hybridization.
paper_structure: The paper first uses DFT to identify the discrepancy between surface and bulk electronic structures. It then constructs a double-layer tight-binding model to microscopically analyze the origins of the observed flat bands, contrasting the interlayer-dependent A-lift with the intralayer-dependent bump-like feature.
why_interesting: The explicit separation of coupling mechanisms (interlayer vs. intralayer) to explain emergent correlated states like flat bands is highly relevant for understanding strongly correlated materials where dimensionality and coupling geometry dictate electronic properties.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) side view and (b) top view of FeSn kagome lattice with unit cell indicated by black line

FIG. 2. DFT band structures and projected density of states (PDOS) of kagome FeSn under different magnetic configurations: (a) antiferromagnetic (AFM), (b) ferromagnetic (FM), and (c) nonmagnetic (NM) states. The left panels show the spin-resolved band structures, and the right panels show the corresponding Fe-d and Sn-p projected density of states. The black dashed horizontal line marks the Fermi level. The highlighted regions indicate the flat-band-related features discussed in the text: the A-lift feature is marked by blue rectangles, and the bump-like feature is marked by red rectangles. The blue dashed horizontal lines indicate the energy level of each flat-band feature.

FIG. 3. Comparison of the electronic structures and Brillouin zones of the primitive 1c cell and doubled 2c supercell. (a) FM and NM band structures calculated using the 1c and 2c cells. (b) Schematic Brillouin zones illustrating the folding along kz. Doubling the lattice periodicity along c halves the Brillouin zone in the out-of-plane direction. The primitive basal Γ−M−K−Γ plane remains at kz = 0, whereas the primitive zone-boundary points A1c, L1c, and H1c at kz = π/c fold onto Γ, M, and K, respectively, in the 2c Brillouin zone. The points A2c, L2c, and H2c define the zone-boundary plane of the doubled cell at kz = π/2c.

FIG. 4. Double-layer tight-binding structure of FeSn. The colored bonds indicate the hopping channels included in the model: intralayer Fe–Fe hopping (blue), interlayer Fe–Fe hop- ping (purple), intralayer Fe–Sn hopping (orange), interlayer Fe–Sn hopping (green), and intralayer Sn–Sn hopping (grey).

FIG. 5. Representative tight-binding candidates for the A-lift flat-band feature. The blue bands indicate the tracked bands selected by the A-lift score, and the projected density of states is shown beside each band structure. (a) FM-like configuration with strong interlayer Fe–Fe hopping, |α| = 1, and absent intralayer Fe–Sn hopping, βintra = 0. The selected band remains nearly flat along the basal-plane Γ–M–K–Γ path and shows an energy lift near the A point. (b) AFM-like configuration under the same hopping condition. The layer-dependent Fe onsite energies break the equivalence between the two kagome layers and reduce the A-point lift.
